To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Draft for Brian: Monday conversation with the Embakasi casuals

Brian,

This is a Sunday briefing for Monday morning. The aim is to be clear, take responsibility and avoid promising a time we can’t keep. Please read it through before you speak with the casuals.

What happened with Friday’s pay

The fortnightly pay file was rejected by the bank because it did not meet the bank’s new file-template requirements. No payments in that file were processed. Finance did not see the rejection alert until after 5pm, by which time the bank cut-off had passed. This is our mistake, not the casuals’ fault. They did nothing wrong, and we should not go in defensive or suggest otherwise.

Management has approved paying the affected casuals by M-Pesa instead. The current expectation from Finance is that the money will be on phones by Monday at 11am. That is the realistic estimate; do not promise an earlier time or present 11am as guaranteed. Finance still has to complete the M-Pesa batch, including the approved float top-up, and Payroll needs to confirm numbers for some people.

Management has also approved KES 500 per person for Monday lunch and fare for every casual on the affected list, paid in the same M-Pesa batch. The company will cover the M-Pesa charges; nothing will be deducted from anyone’s payment. Don’t guess or announce a fare amount that hasn’t been confirmed.

What you can say

You can apologise on management’s behalf, in person. Keep it direct: “Friday’s pay did not go through because our payment file was rejected and we did not catch the alert in time. We’re sorry. This was our mistake, not yours. We’re moving payment to M-Pesa. The current expectation is that it will reach phones by 11am Monday, and Finance is working on the batch. The approved lunch and fare support will be included, and M-Pesa charges will not be deducted.”

Be honest if someone asks whether 11am is certain: it is the current expected time, not a guarantee. If you learn that the timing or payment plan has changed, tell me on WhatsApp before I board. I’m up from 4:30am. Don’t fill gaps with guesses; check with Finance or Payroll and come back with an update.

Monday morning

You’ll be at the depot at 5:30am. Keep your tone calm and listen before trying to resolve everything in front of the group. This is not a situation to approach as if the casuals caused the problem.

Ouma is upset, but that does not make him a bad man. Speak to him privately first, before addressing the whole group. Let him explain what people are worried about, including rent and the risk of another missed promise. Don’t make the private conversation sound like a warning or an attempt to single him out. Then speak to the group plainly, apologise, explain the payment plan and give them room to ask questions.

Peninah will be at Embakasi from 7:30am with the list. She has confirmed 198 numbers and could not reach 14 people, mostly new loaders from the Athi River intake. She will check those 14 numbers face to face so Payroll can correct them. She can also print payslips for anyone who wants one. Don’t imply that someone whose number needs checking has been excluded from the affected list or that their payment has already been sent.

If the group refuses to load the Kisumu trucks

The trucks need to leave by 9am to make the mill’s offloading slot. Take the concern seriously, but don’t promise that a conversation will make the trucks leave on time or tell people to load before you know what is happening with their payment.

Our procedure says a work stoppage is not a grievance channel. If there is a stoppage, it must be handled jointly by Operations and HR. Bring in the shift supervisor and HR, keep the discussion orderly, and make a clear record of what was raised and what response was given. The usual grievance route is first to the shift supervisor, then to HR within 48 hours. Explain that route without using it to dismiss what people are saying now.

Do not threaten anyone with dismissal or make threats about contracts. No one is to be dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day of a stoppage. Don’t argue, retaliate, or try to resolve this alone. Keep the focus on the facts, the immediate discussion and the joint Ops/HR process. If the 9am departure is at risk, update the relevant Operations and HR people promptly so they can manage the transport and mill-slot implications while the conversation continues.

Keep the message consistent: we own the payment mistake; the current M-Pesa expectation is 11am Monday, not earlier and not guaranteed; the approved lunch and fare support is in the same batch, with charges covered by the company; and any stoppage is handled jointly by Operations and HR, without threats.
